rationale: Greek loanword ἀναβιβάζων 'the ascending one' — technical astronomical term for the lunar node (caput/cauda draconis). Used here in the dual ⲡⲁⲛⲁⲃⲓⲃⲁⲍⲱⲛ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the two Anabibazons' = ascending and descending nodes, the two virtual points (not actual stars) that complete the seven-fold planetary inventory of Manichaean astrology. Identified here with Fire and Pleasure, as offspring of the Dry-One (Father) and the Abomination (Mother).

Variant orthography of accumulated ⲍⲏⲁⲟⲛⲏ < ἡδονή 'pleasure'. Lyc ⲍ for ζ/η, with metathesis. Standard Manichaean cosmological feminine principle paired with Fire (ⲥⲉⲧⲉ) as the maternal-feminine cosmic pole.

Lycopolitan ⲕⲟⲟⲍ = Sahidic ⲕⲟⲟϩ 'corner, angle' (Crum 137a). In the present astrological context refers to one of the four cosmic corners/quarters into which the twelve zodiacal signs are distributed three at a time — i.e., the four astrological trigones (fire/earth/air/water).
Greek ὑδροχόος 'water-pourer' = the constellation/zodiac-sign Aquarius. Lyc ⲍⲩⲇ- for ⲩⲇⲣ- with vowel-dilation. The Greek constellation-name retained as proper name.

Greek κλῆρος 'lot, allotted portion' — astrologically the assigned trigone-quadrant. Lycopolitan ⲕⲗⲁⲭⲉ shows ⲭ for ⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲥ → ⲕⲗⲁⲭⲉ (vowel-shift and consonant simplification). Used here interchangeably with ⲥⲁ 'side' for the four astrological lots.
Lycopolitan rendering of Greek Ἑρμῆς with ⲍ-onset (cf. accumulated ⲍⲉⲣⲙⲏⲛⲉⲩⲉ for ἑρμηνεύειν — same ⲍ-for-Greek-spiritus pattern). The planet Mercury, here assigned to the world of Water.
Greek Κρόνος. The planet Saturn, here assigned to the world of Darkness as the slowest and outermost of the classical planets.
Greek Ἄρης. The planet Mars, here assigned to the world of Wind.
Greek Ζεύς. The planet Jupiter, here begotten from the world of Smoke (= mind).
Greek Ἀφροδίτη. The planet Venus, here from the world of Fire — the only feminine planet, paired naturally with the feminine fire-principle Hēdonē.
